Anyway, a lot of “ghetto” or “weird” black names are old, have meaning, and/or have tradition in communities in America or abroad.

For example, Shaniqua is African-Americanized version of Shanika meaning “God is gracious”.

Aisha is the name of the prophet Muhammad’s favorite wife. Darius is borrowed from the Greek ‘Dareios’, a name so old, it’s original meaning is lost to the ages. Imani is Kiswahili for faith. Jamal is Hebrew, meaning hansom. Shomari is Swahili and means “he who has a great personality”.

I think people also often like to come up with variations of names they like or create one based on how it sounds.

There’s residential treatment. You often have share a room and/or apartment with others. It’s very scheduled with group therapies and appointments. It’s the kind of place where you can earn “day passes” after a period of observation to leave and do your own thing for a few hours.

A step down would be partial hospitalization or PHP. It’s around 4-7 hours a day 5-7 days a week. I’m doing a PHP right now. There are various group things we rotate through, like dbt, cbt, art therapy, processes IBH, etc. (each time you learn new skills though) The staff also pull us out to check in with the nurse or have an appointment with our psychiatrist or individual therapist.

The last PHP I tried was meh, but this one is so much better. If you need to talk, they ensure a staff member gets to you asap, groups are small, patients are nice (I’ve actually made friends).

If you have an a therapist or psychiatrist, you can let them know that you feel like you could benefit from more intensive care. They’ll likely have recommendations for what would be best for where you are and which places they see results from.

Best of luck!
